headline: Cost discipline lifts margins despite a flat top line
summary_short: Total revenue rose to $2,160M (+1.0% y/y, +3.3% q/q) as self-pay rate increases and advertising growth offset a smaller average subscriber base; income from operations climbed to $472M (+29.3% y/y) on lower G&A and restructuring costs, while diluted EPS of $0.70 was up 22.8% y/y but down 2.8% q/q.
summary_long: Adjusted EBITDA rose to $691M (+3.4% y/y) on higher subscriber and advertising revenue plus lower cost of services, product & technology, and G&A, partly offset by higher sales & marketing and subscriber-acquisition costs tied to next-generation chipset migration. Free cash flow jumped to $593M (+47.5% y/y) on the EBITDA gain, lower cash taxes, and favorable payment timing. SiriusXM added 90,000 net self-pay/promotional subscribers versus a 66,000 net loss a year ago, helped by companion-subscription and retention initiatives. The board paid a $0.27/share quarterly dividend in the quarter and repurchased $28M of stock year-to-date ($996M remains authorized); no quantified FY2026 guidance range was reiterated in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow both grew as disciplined cost management and higher subscriber/advertising revenue outweighed higher subscriber-acquisition and sales & marketing costs tied to the chipset migration.

Subscriber revenue rose 1% on self-pay rate increases, partly offset by fewer average subscribers; advertising grew on sports demand and podcast/programmatic growth; equipment revenue fell 22% on higher hardware memory costs.

Operating income rose $107M y/y as $30M lower G&A (reduced legal costs) and $101M lower impairment/restructuring charges outweighed $44M higher D&A tied to a shortened useful life on the Sirius FM-6 satellite.

Net income tracked the operating-income gain but was tempered by a $59M swing in other (expense) income, to a $48M loss from a $15M gain a year ago, mainly unrealized losses on debt measured at fair value.
Diluted EPS grew roughly in line with net income on a smaller diluted share count (342M vs 357M shares a year ago) as convertible-note dilution declined.

Growth was driven by higher subscriber and advertising revenue plus lower cost of services, product & technology, and G&A from cost discipline, partly offset by higher sales & marketing and subscriber-acquisition costs.
The jump reflected higher Adjusted EBITDA, lower cash taxes paid, and favorable timing of vendor payments and capital expenditures.

Self-pay net additions improved on growth in value-add initiatives (companion subscriptions, continuous service, dealer extended-duration plans) and lower vehicle-related/non-pay churn, partly offset by slightly lower conversion rates.
